final_rationale: The verdict changes only because the Actor narrowed the claim to match the admissible record; no new admissible evidence was added. The evidence supports that aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, but it also shows an unresolved weakness in a named launch use case, a draft mitigation missing required approval elements, and an unresolved model-card disclosure question. Under the policy text, those facts do not support clean certification without material caveats. They do support, at most, a caveated compliance position if the remaining limitation is explicitly disclosed and handled through proper governance. That is the key distinction: the caveated position is proportionate to the evidence, while any claim that the issue is already resolved or already covered by an approved mitigation remains unsupported.
remaining_concerns: The legal intake triage slice remains below target in a named launch use case area, concentrated in privilege-sensitive routing.
The mitigation runbook is still draft and lacks at least a named owner and alert threshold, so the policy-standard approved mitigation predicate is not met.
The model-card record still contains an unresolved question about whether this issue must be disclosed as a material limitation.
The record still does not show a final disclosure decision or approved risk acceptance before launch.
